A penetration test is an authorized, simulated attack performed to evaluate a system's security by identifying its vulnerabilities and strengths, enabling a complete risk assessment. Tests can be white, black, or gray box and target various areas like networks or web applications. The practice is defined by bodies like the UK NCSC and is mandated by standards like PCI DSS, supported by frameworks such as OSSTMM and PTES. The concept originated in the 1960s with concerns about time-sharing system security, leading to formal studies and reports identifying penetration as a major threat. Modern developments include Penetration Testing as a Service (PTaaS), offering platforms as an alternative to consultant-led engagements.
